previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and chronic back pain was admitted for recurrent nausea and vomiting. She had tried Zofran at home without success and presented with worsening symptoms and back pain. IV antiemetics provided relief, and she tolerated advancement to a regular diabetic diet. Her blood glucose remained stable except for one episode of mild hypoglycemia, managed with food. The insulin regimen was unchanged. Gabapentin was started for back pain as a required trial before lidocaine patch approval. She was advised to use Ativan instead of Zofran for future nausea episodes. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned with her new care team, including the Chronic Pain Service.
problems: Diabetes with unspecified complication, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year-old female with a past medical history of poorly

chronic pain, multiple recent admissions for vomiting who 
presented with nausea, vomiting, back pain and abdominal pain.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
==============
# Nausea/Vomiting, Diarrhea: patient has an extensive history of 
recurrent episodes of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. She 
has had almost weekly admissions for this for the past few 
months and had inpatient work-ups with poor outpatient 
follow-up. She was initially thought to have gatric dysmotility 
in ___ and at that time had a normal gastric emptying study. On 
susbequent admissions she was evaluated by psychiatry and 
thought to have ""flooding"" induced by extreme anxiety which 
manifested as nausea and vomiting. She was also found to have 
grade 1 varices on EGD in ___ and biopsy confirmed gastritis 
and + H pylori at that time for which she was treated with 
2-week course of triple therapy. On this admission, patient had 
blood sugar of 600 but was not in DKA. She was advanced the same 
day to regular diet which she tolerated well, and she did not 
have recurrent diarrhea or vomiting. Her initial symptoms may 
have been due to gastroenteritis from eating potato salad prior 
to admission or to her hyperglycemia. There was no indication of 
a significant psychiatric component contributing to this 
presentation. We performed a repeat gastric emptying study which 
was normal. As below, patient's blood sugars were very labile 
throughout the hospitalization and ___ was consulted to 
recommend an outpatient regimen. Patient will need GI follow-up 
which was scheduled to repeat EGD for evaluation of varices and 
to confirm eradication of H pylori. She will be establishing 
care with a PCP in ___ few days with the help of social work.

present 12.8% with eAG>300. She is on lantus and sliding scale 
at home and reports checking her finger sticks qachs with 
readings in the 200's. She relates many of her episodes of 
nausea and vomiting to elevated blood sugar though is not aware 
of precipitants of this. She does carb counting at home, but 
during the hospitalization had several instances of critically 
high readings after consuming ___ ice, etc. without being 
aware of the glucose load in these foods. She also had 
hypoglycemia of ___ ___ in the morning which was attributed to 
overtreating high readings with humalog throughout the night. Pt 
was counselled on diabetic diet and evaluated by ___ who 
recommended continuing lantus at 28 units and decreasing carb 
counting ratio to 1:12 with coverage of 1 units humalog for each 
elevation in blood sugar of 40 over 140. She is not able to 
follow up at ___ due to many previously missed appointments 
but should have follow up through ___ after establishing care 
with a PCP. Her insulin supplies were called in to her pharmacy 
on discharge.
.
# Social issues: Patient has been admitted 4 times in the past 
month with multiple previous admissions and has a long history 
of depression/anxiety, non-compliance, and chronic pain. She has 
difficulty keeping outpatient appointments with GI, PCP, 
___, pain clinic, and ___ though social work had been 
trying to establish a multidisciplinary care team for her. On 
this admission, patient expressed the desire to start taking 
care of her health and to try to keep her appointments. She is 
attempting to transition all of her care to ___. She was set up 
with a new PCP on discharge and social work will accompany her 
to this appointment. At that time, they will help set her up 
with the ___ social worker and therapist. She was also given an 
appointment to follow-up with GI. Patient needs intensive 
diabetic management as above, and close follow-up is crucial for 
her. She should continue to follow with social work for ongoing 
support and improved adherence to outpatient appointments, which 
will hopefully reduce her readmission rate.
.
# Anxiety/Psychiatric issues: patient has a long history of 
anxiety, traumatic events, and depression but has not been 
followed as an outpatient. Some of her nausea/vomiting episodes 
were attributed to ""flooding"" and panic attacks in the past. She 
has previously been tried on SSRIs, ativan, and clonidine in 
various combinations but currently only taking ativan as needed 
for anxiety. She did not have active SI/HI on this admission, 
and did not display significant psychiatric symptoms other than 
having mild anxiety and tearfulness on admission. She was 
evaluated by psychiatry for possibly initiating SSRI therapy as 
an inpatient given poor adherence to outpatient follow-up, but 
they thought there was no indication for immediate medical 
therapy as she was not having any active issues. Social work saw 
the patient and will help connect her to the social workers and 
therapist at ___. They will be meeting patient at her PCP

She was referred for follow-up with outpatient pain clinic but 
has not kept her appointments there. We continued her on 
tylenol, gabapentin and lidoderm patch. She did not require any
